units.text: INT. BEEKEEPER'S KITCHEN - MORNING
Honey-gold light slants through a window crusted with propolis.
On the table, a cracked jar leaks slow amber across oilcloth.
FLORIAN ACHTERBERG (70s, veil pushed back, hands like roots) stands rigid at the stove.
His daughter MAREN (40s, city coat, car keys still in her fist) has not sat down.
At the table, her son EZRA (9, scabbed elbows) hides behind a comic book, while his aunt ODALYS (50s, flour on her apron) pretends to knead dough.
You sold the north hives without telling me.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: They were mine to sell.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: Maren, sit. There's tea.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: I don't want tea. Dad, those were Mom's.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: Your mother is dead eleven years. The bees don't know it.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: Are we fighting?
units.name: EZRA

units.text: No, sweetheart. We're discussing.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: I drove six hours. I thought you were sick.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: I am old. It's the same thing.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: You could have asked me.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: And you would have said keep them. And I would have kept them. And they would have died, because I can't lift the supers anymore.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: Silence.
A single bee drifts across the room and lands on the leaking jar.
Ezra, bring me the dish towel.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: He does.
Maren sits at last.
Florian turns from the stove, picks up the jar, and sets it in front of her.
Taste.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: Dad.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: Taste it.
units.name: FLORIAN

units.text: She dips a finger.
Her face softens as she tastes, and she covers her mouth with her wrist.
It's hers.
units.name: MAREN

units.text: The last of the north. I saved it for you.
units.name: FLORIAN
